quiz.q: Where did the first cheetahs come from?
quiz.why: Right. The first eight came from Namibia and were released at Kuno on 17 September 2022; twelve from South Africa followed in February 2023.

steps.text: An expert committee to guide it

claims.claim: The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952
On 28 January 2020 the Supreme Court allowed the introduction of African cheetahs to a suitable habitat in India (Centre for Environment Law, WWF v. Union of India)
The Court said it would amount to an 'introduction' of the African cheetah, not a re-introduction, and formed a Committee of Experts to guide the process
claims.quote: an 'introduction' of the African Cheetah and not a re-introduction

claims.claim: The first eight cheetahs came from Namibia and were released at Kuno on 17 September 2022 (2022)
Twelve cheetahs arrived from South Africa in February 2023
As of September 2026 India has 52 cheetahs (over fifty, 50+), 32 of them born in India

review_note: All sources are secondary. The SC order text was read through India Environment Portal's summary, not the order PDF. Counts are shown only as 'over fifty, as of September 2026' (sources report 52; others report 57-60 at other dates, so the number moves). 'Most born here' rests on 32 of 52. Left out: cheetah deaths, Gandhi Sagar, Botswana batch (not confirmed), the 2023 SC hearings on deaths.
